He served as a general for the Papal States and the Republic of Venice, notably fighting in the Italian Wars and the Ottoman–Venetian War (1570–1573). He was appointed as the first Marquis of Castiglione del Lago by Pope Pius IV in 1563 and later became a cardinal, though primarily for political and military reasons rather than ecclesiastical ones. He was known for his strategic skill and involvement in conflicts such as the Battle of Lepanto (1571), where he commanded papal galleys.
